messages:
elaine: heads-up, 'OrionEdge' asked for a mixed workload POC next week: chat + embeddings. Target: 99.9 tail <300ms at 60 qps for chat, embeddings ~1200 reqs/min. Want multi-region sweep and cold-start visibility.

samir: sounds good. need shapes: chat lengths and embedding dim/payload. that affects model & quantization choice.

maya: they replied: chat avg ~90 tokens, 95th ~250 tokens; embeddings are plain text ~512 bytes average, can spike. they expect short burst windows up to 200 qps for a few minutes. also asked for hosted vs committed pricing numbers.

jack: ops checklist: run from us-west1 + eu-west1 to replicate their geography. either they provide a service account/agent or we run from our dedicated infra. confirm TLS and KMS if they test Private. also network peering note for EU office.

vivian: security asks: data residency for embeddings, retention policy, whether inputs are logged. they'll need entries in our compliance tracker (SOC21). flag legal for PII clause.

elaine: propose run plan: 1) smoke (10m) validate correctness & responses 2) steady baseline 30m @60 qps 3) spike test ramp to 200 qps for 5m 4) cold-start churn: cycle ~20 worker instances to surface cold KV cache behavior. capture p50/p95/p99 (request + per-token), token/sec, success rate.

samir: model recs: rdx-3b-chat-q8 for chat, rdx-embed-1 for embeddings. rdx-3b-chat-q8 balances mem & latency; I'll prepare a small quant/latency matrix. also will run an internal sim this afternoon to estimate expected p99 for 60 qps and paste results here.

maya: can someone draft the wrk/curl commands I can hand to their infra? ops-bot, can you paste recommended commands + headers?

ops-bot: runbook snippet:
```bash
# chats (simulate streaming chat requests)
wrk -t12 -c60 -d00:30s --latency \n  --script=chat.lua -- https://<PROXY>/v1/chat \n  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \n  --header 'X-Redwood-Debug: trace' \n  --latency
# embeddings
wrk -t8 -c200 -d00:05s --latency \n  --script=embed.lua -- https://<PROXY>/v1/embeddings \n  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \n  --header 'X-Redwood-Debug: trace'
```

jack: remember to enable header X-Redwood-Debug to gather KV cache hit ratios and include trace IDs in payload for tail analysis. also capture GPU util and host-level metrics.

elaine: can we run Thurs 09:00 PT? prospect prefers morning. maya will confirm with them and ask for sample dataset + security contact.

maya: confirming Thurs 09:00 PT with OrionEdge. i'll request sample traffic, expected baseline hours/month, and burst schedule so we can price Dedicated commit. also ask for their security ops contact for the questionnaire.

samir: metric checklist to report: p50/p95/p99 request latency, p50/p95/p99 per-token latency, tokens/sec, success rate (HTTP 2xx), cold-start count, KV cache hit %, GPU util, and any observed tail cause (GC, network, model swap).

vivian: pricing: they want (A) hosted estimate for steady 60 qps and (B) committed Dedicated pool price supporting baseline + burst to 200 qps with a 99.9% tail SLA. finance will need monthly sustained hours and burst hours.

maya: i'll draft (A) after we have baseline numbers; (B) depends on expected sustained usage. if they can share monthly h baseline + burst hours i can give a better number.

elaine: risk: if embeddings contain PII we must enable no-retention mode and update contract. legal needs to review.

samir: i'll post quick internal sim numbers for rdx-3b-chat-q8 shortly so we have an expectation for p99 before the POC.

jack: note: cross-region runs will inflate latencies if peering isn't setup. ask them to confirm VPN/peering or we should run regionally isolated tests.

maya: noted. will collect peering info and post back. will also attach sample payloads once they share.

elaine: great work. drop short updates here only so we keep thread clean. :thumbsup:
